sections.title: Identity, scope and research verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Pramodini Medicare Limited, NSE PRAMODINI, ISIN INE2JG601017, CIN U85110AP2000PLC035231, operates diagnostic imaging and laboratories, not inpatient hospitals. It was incorporated in September 2000, changed to public-company status in November 2025 and first appears in the official listed tape on 19 August 2026. The analytical cutoff is 20 October 2026; the authenticated reference quote is the 19 October close of ₹115.10, not a live executable bid. Financials are nominal INR crore unless stated. This report was researched after the cutoff using documents dated on or before it.

A genuine scaling business is visible: revenue expanded from ₹18.56cr in FY21 to ₹62.29cr in FY26, with MRI/CT/private-hospital and PSU activity contributing. However, an unresolved ₹9.20cr difference between the FY25 CARO guarantee total and the latest prospectus disclosures is material relative to equity and available free cash. This is an inconsistency requiring reconciliation, not an allegation of fraud. Vista recoverability, bank-return controls and old equipment payables compound the need for clarification.

BQS and GQS are diagnostic assessments, excluded from quality rankings while G2 is on Hold. R and IAS are NS. Neither an apparently modest earnings multiple nor a conditional spreadsheet outcome cures reliability. The report provides a five-year, cash-linked scenario model but no actionable target price, ordinary expected return or recommendation to transact.

sections.title: Business model and diagnostic unit economics
sections.text:
Radiology generated ₹60.4498cr, 97.05% of FY26 sales; laboratory services contributed ₹1.4754cr and new nuclear medicine ₹0.3623cr. The business operates through hospital partnerships, government PPP contracts, PSU O&M contracts and private centres. These have different payer and capital intensity: PSU equipment can be provided by the contracting principal with rent-free premises, whereas owned MRI/CT machines require substantial company capital. Aggregating them as identical hospitals or applying bed occupancy/ARPOB would be misleading.

Total procedures rose from 254,765 to 474,419 in FY26. MRI volumes rose from 95,426 to 128,566; CT from 45,815 to 97,880; X-ray from 8,555 to 110,583. Laboratory volume fell from 53,678 to 50,016. Consequently, blended sales per procedure fell from roughly ₹1,501 to ₹1,313 despite 62.9% sales growth. That is a mix-sensitive realization measure, not proof of a like-for-like price cut. Nuclear volumes are only 257 procedures, and radiology includes teleradiology, so counting procedures alone overstates comparability.

The issuer lists 16 centres across 14 cities and seven states, but Manjeri was not yet operational and Bangalore was only an LOI for proposed development. The list therefore is not 16 mature earning units. Eight CT systems, workforce expansion from 54 to 161 permanent employees, and rising procedures substantiate physical scaling, but installed MRI/CT hours, utilization, payer-specific realization, centre EBITDA, renewal success and mature/new-site ROIC are not sufficiently disclosed for precise site forecasts. They are requested operating evidence, not invented metrics.

sections.title: Competitive position, contracts and accessible market
sections.text:
The practical competitive assets are medical referral relationships, reliable diagnostic delivery, hospital access, qualified personnel and the ability to procure and operate expensive imaging equipment. These can create local switching friction, but there is no independently established national market share or proprietary technology monopoly. MOAT is mixed, not inferred from the brand, margin or IPO subscription. Tender pricing, hospital partners and service quality constrain pricing freedom; equipment is available to competing operators.

FY26 PPP revenue was ₹33.7507cr (54.19%), private-hospital partnerships ₹12.9676cr, private centres ₹11.0392cr and PSU O&M ₹4.5300cr. Combining PPP and PSU gives 61.46% public-sector-related revenue. FY25 PPP dependence was approximately 70.88%, so revenue diversification improved, but payer timing remains a central economic exposure. These categories are not customer concentration measures. Centre and counterparty concentration need separate contract-level monitoring; public-sector demand does not guarantee prompt payment.

The accessible reinvestment opportunity is the specified equipment programme at Hubli, Manjeri, Bangalore and Vijayawada, rather than a headline India-wide healthcare TAM. Modelled mature new sales at 0.35–0.85 times ₹45.1485cr equipment investment imply ₹15.80–38.38cr incremental annual revenue, with commissioning and ramp delays. These are analyst productivity assumptions, not contracted revenue or equipment-capacity guarantees. Management's narrative is supported by volume growth and new service models, but no verified unit-capacity denominator supports extrapolating national market share.

sections.title: Historical growth, comparability and earnings bridge
sections.text:
Six annual financial rows are retained, not just an IPO three-year snapshot. Revenue FY21–FY26 is ₹18.5605/25.0753/30.5814/35.2295/38.2377/62.2875cr. The five-year CAGR is 27.4%; the three-year check is 26.8%. The FY21 pandemic period is a possible distortion, but the comparable three-year result is very similar. REV therefore uses the five-year 20–30% band, score 8, with no trajectory bonus. Latest FY26 growth of 62.9% followed FY25 growth of only 8.5%, so one unusually strong full year is not treated as an enduring acceleration. There is no verified H1 FY27 result at the cutoff and no fabricated TTM.

Parent AS23 reporting is preserved. The FY21 file's website category does not turn standalone statements into consolidated accounts; FY22 original associates and April DRHP FY23 are separately labelled. Final July-restated FY24–26 figures supersede earlier restatement versions. Five-year PAT CAGR is withheld because original and restated profit treatments differ. The stable latest three years show operating EBIT ₹11.1452/16.6854/23.5126cr, EBITDA ₹15.5347/20.9662/30.9035cr and attributable PAT ₹6.9301/11.0276/17.3773cr.

FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 49.61% from 54.83%, despite scale, as staffing, new service mix and running costs expanded. Gross profit is ND because the service-cost split is not a complete consistent gross-margin presentation. Other income is separated, not capitalized as recurring operating profit. Related-party interest alone was ₹0.9271cr in FY26. Deducting its assumed 25% after-tax benefit gives PAT ₹16.6820cr, an illustrative normalization rather than audited restatement. Future IPO-funded cash interest is not used to disguise operating returns.

sections.title: Governance, ownership and capital allocation
sections.text:
The controlling doctors and promoter group operate related healthcare entities, creating useful industry experience alongside material capital-allocation conflicts. FY26 director remuneration of ₹0.60cr is only 3.45% of attributable profit; remuneration itself is not the main issue. More important are ₹7.3369cr advanced to loss-making associate Vista, ₹1.3021cr advance and ₹0.1632cr expense receivable from Infer, and guarantees for another group company. Infer balances remain in the operating-asset bridge and are not separately added as an investment asset. Vista is excluded from free cash and base terminal recoveries.

Vista's carrying equity investment is nil, while cumulative unrecognized associate losses are ₹6.0529cr. AS23's investment-loss limit does not by itself establish that the separate demand loan is worthless or recoverable. No full additional associate loss is automatically consolidated, and no NCI is invented. The closing Vista loan is arithmetically consistent with ₹5.4525cr opening + ₹1.05cr new lending + ₹0.9271cr interest less ₹0.09271cr assumed 10% TDS. This strongly suggests net interest capitalization, but is an inference needing lender and counterparty confirmation, not verified cash collection despite the RPT label.

The IPO raised ₹63.13944cr gross fresh capital; ₹5.90472cr OFS proceeds went to sellers, not the company. The fresh issue expanded shares by 32.05%, reducing existing ownership percentage by 24.27%. The bonus issue was noncash and is not financing. Post-issue shares of 22,045,595 are authenticated by the dated security master. There is no verified new post-cutoff dilution included in the base. Promoter lock-ins and market-maker holdings reduce practical float, but current pledge/surveillance completeness is not claimed. The auditor change in October 2025 is explicitly explained as obtaining a peer-reviewed auditor for the IPO, not assumed to be a scope-dispute resignation.

sections.title: Financial reliability and audit annexures
sections.text:
The FY25 original main opinions were unmodified. The standalone CARO says loan terms were stipulated, accounts regular, no overdue loan amounts, no debt default, no reported fraud, and no current-asset-secured limits above ₹5cr. Those are meaningful dated counterfacts. Audit-trail testing reports operation and no tampering; the report's retention wording is preserved as a limitation rather than a separate assurance. IFC reporting was explicitly not applicable, so there is no clean IFC effectiveness opinion to cite. Full original FY26 statutory main report/CARO/IFC/audit-trail annexures were not located on the issuer's financial and annual-report pages. The later examination report's absence of qualifications requiring restatement does not substitute for those original annexures.

The material contradiction is specific: FY25 standalone CARO page 7 states total guarantees outstanding of ₹14.15cr. Its notes identify ₹4.95cr to Sri Ram, and the final prospectus shows ₹4.95cr corporate guarantee plus smaller bank guarantees. A ₹9.20cr corporate-guarantee reconciliation or extinguishment evidence was not found. The source text was visually verified; this is not an OCR artefact. Stress cases use ₹14.15cr as an alternative total, never ₹14.15cr plus ₹4.95cr.

The latest restatement also states that monthly current-asset returns were not submitted to banks, so reconciliation could not be assessed; it does not quantify a bank-return mismatch. Some sanction documents were being retrieved, with accounts relying on statements/schedules. These observations differ in period and scope from FY25 CARO and are not labelled a direct contradiction. Original-to-final FY25 PAT changed ₹11.5579→11.0276cr and equity ₹38.5215→35.7745cr; FY24 PAT ₹7.1259→6.9301cr and equity ₹26.9637→24.7469cr. Depreciation lives, gratuity, finance charges, tax/TDS and opening repairs are explicitly bridged. That transparency is positive, but balances subject to confirmation and the guarantee difference keep G2 on Hold.

sections.title: Cash realization and working capital
sections.text:
Reported FY24–26 cumulative CFO of ₹57.37cr is 1.62 times PAT. This headline is not a clean collection statistic. The cash-flow presentation records gross PPE additions as investing uses while allowing changes in equipment creditors into CFO. Those creditors rose from ₹0.7831cr at FY23 to ₹18.2876cr at FY26. Removing ₹17.50cr of supplier financing leaves CFO ₹39.86cr. Excluding FD releases and adding back only identified prepaid IPO fees produces ₹37.82cr, or 1.07 times PAT. This is adequate cumulative conversion, not persistent cash failure, so the weak-cash GQS ceiling is explicitly not triggered.

The paired capex reclassification preserves FCF: FY26 reported CFO ₹25.3905cr less gross asset purchases ₹29.8118cr equals −₹4.4213cr; operating CFO excluding equipment-creditor growth is ₹10.0452cr and corresponding cash capex ₹14.4665cr, giving the same deficit. Calling all ₹29.8118cr cash paid while also treating unpaid suppliers as true operating cash would misread the economics. Actual supplier settlement is an opening funding obligation, not fresh project capex twice.

Receivable days improved from roughly 186 in FY24 to 107 in FY25 and 102 in FY26, but balances over six months jumped from ₹1.1711cr to ₹5.9263cr, 34.1% of FY26 receivables. All are considered good without a doubtful-debt provision in the restatement. Inventory and short supplier advances also absorbed cash. The ₹4.95cr old manpower payable fell to nil; that cash release/settlement pattern should not repeat mechanically. CASH 6 reflects both the multi-year conversion evidence and worsening ageing, without duplicating the guarantee concern across unrelated factors.

sections.title: Balance sheet, cash availability and survival
sections.text:
March 2026 cash equivalents were ₹6.3690cr, distinct from ₹0.0680cr other bank deposits and ₹0.8908cr long deposits. ₹0.8426cr of the latter was lien-marked; none of these deposits, Vista loans or the ₹4cr hospital-division acquisition advance is treated as opening free cash. Bank/NBFC debt totals ₹17.8481cr, including ₹4.0847cr current maturities. Adding ₹18.2876cr unpaid equipment creditors gives a much fuller financing obligation than a bank-debt-only ratio. Capital creditors are included in invested capital, and deducted through cash settlement rather than again at the terminal equity bridge.

The fresh IPO net allocation is approximately ₹55.9060cr: ₹45.1485cr for specified equipment and ₹10.7575cr general corporate/unidentified acquisitions. Equipment proceeds are a separate eligible cash pot, not available for unrelated creditors or guarantees. ₹0.2397cr of offer fees was already prepaid, so only remaining fees are deducted when modelling IPO receipt. ₹1.61cr current capital advances and the ₹4cr acquisition advance are already paid assets, not future cash uses recharged in the forecast. The ₹45.1485cr programme is the stated outstanding amount after its own earlier advance, and is not grossed up by that advance again.

Axis had issued ₹14.31cr LCs to equipment vendors but the term loan was not disbursed at restatement; HDFC facilities were sanctioned but not disbursed. Neither is invented as cash received. If the LCs convert, vendor liability should convert to debt, not count as both fresh free cash and unpaid suppliers. Old tax ₹1.6968cr, statutory dues ₹0.3486cr and gratuity ₹0.4628cr are separately settled once in the model. No historical default is inferred from an analyst cash reserve or assumed creditor payment date. G3 is Conditional: plausible financeability exists, but repayment/guarantee documentation and actual IPO deployment are needed to remove timing dependence.

sections.title: Incremental capital efficiency and execution
sections.text:
The stable FY24–26 operating bridge uses normalized 25% tax on EBIT and invested capital defined as net PPE + operating NWC + paid capital/acquisition advances + operating deposits. Financial investments, excess cash and Vista loans are separately identified; equipment creditors are not allowed to reduce operating capital. Keeping the idle ₹4cr acquisition advance in the denominator avoids rewarding capital not yet producing earnings. Incremental NOPAT was ₹9.28cr on ₹47.76cr additional operating capital, giving 19.4%; including related loans lowers this to 18.4%. Reclassifying recurring bank fees into operating expense gives 19.2%. CAP 6 is supported by this measured organic multi-year bridge, not present ROCE alone; it is not forced NS merely because private centre-level cohorts are absent.

This is an endpoint estimate, not proof every new centre earns that return. FY26 equipment additions and late commissioning are not mature, working-capital needs are payer-sensitive, and associate losses are not part of the operating return. Against an illustrative 11–14% capital-cost range the historical return suggests positive reinvestment value, but materially below a risk-free compounding promise. The model explicitly pays for incremental legacy capacity and maintenance as well as the IPO programme.

Observable execution milestones are stronger than speculative guidance: FY26 procedures and permanent staff expanded sharply; private-partnership and PSU revenue became significant; 3T MRI/CT equipment at Belagavi created large vendor balances. In contrast, Manjeri was not operating, Bangalore had an LOI rather than demonstrated earnings, and the newly funded programme had no post-IPO utilization report at cutoff. The lead manager's visit covered two Vijayawada premises, not independent verification of all 16 listed centres. EXEC 6 gives credit for delivered volumes without treating planned machines as delivered cash returns.

sections.title: Five-year operating, reinvestment and funding model
sections.text:
The model runs from 31 March 2026 cash to the 19 October 2026 entry and exactly 19 October 2031 exit, using actual days/365.25 and no post-terminal receipts. Monthly and event-date rows, pre-entry rows and five investment-year aggregates are embedded. Revenue is a legacy volume/yield path plus equipment-cohort output: base legacy volume growth 7%, flat yield, new mature sales 0.60× equipment capital, three-month commissioning lag and 18-month ramp. Bear uses 2% volume, −2% yield, 0.35× productivity and slower commissioning; bull 11%, +1%, 0.85× and faster ramp. The planned spend is seven equal tranches; delay stresses move the actual payments and revenue ramps together.

Base legacy/new EBITDA margins are 45%/42%, before explicitly retained recurring bank/LC/BG fees; rent, equipment rents, staffing, consumables, repairs and administration remain throughout. Depreciation reflects existing assets plus new and growth assets; maintenance capex is 7% of sales and additional legacy growth investment is linked to incremental sales at 1.5× capital turnover. Receivable days are 110 plus 24 other net-working-capital days. Bear combines 150 collection days, lower margins, 9% maintenance and a ₹4.95cr guarantee call. Tax, interest, principal, growth/maintenance capex, positive NWC and old claims are pre-funded before interval net operating receipts. No apparent annual surplus is allowed to hide an intra-period shortfall.

The assumption that old equipment creditors are fully settled on 31 October 2026 is important and is NOT a source-confirmed extension of credit. June and August settlement sensitivities test pre-entry and pre-IPO exposure. IPO cash is dated to listing as an explicit bank-release assumption, with actual allotment independently evidenced but bank release unverified. Under the ₹2cr reserve the base trough is ₹1.4778cr, a ₹0.5222cr shortfall, so both ordinary and non-rescue conditional base returns are null. Reducing the analyst reserve to ₹1cr funds the path; this is a sensitivity, not evidence that the lower reserve is appropriate. Bear's ₹10.33cr floor gap needs an explicit rescue. Rescue issues whole shares at a 30% discount plus 5% fees, before interval uses, with dilution distinguished from share expansion.

sections.title: Valuation, dilution and reverse expectations
sections.text:
At ₹115.10 and 22,045,595 issued shares, market value is ₹253.7448cr. FY26 attributable profit translates to ₹7.8824 EPS on current shares, versus the historical weighted-average/bonus-adjusted published EPS. The resulting 14.60× P/E is not a forecast return. Excluding the assumed after-tax benefit of related-party interest gives 15.21×. Current issued-share dilution should not be confused with cash-generating earnings growth or retroactively treated as the FY26 statutory denominator.

The return model values terminal operating EBITDA at 6×/8×/10× in bear/base/bull, subtracts remaining debt, retains the operating cash reserve, and adds only signed unencumbered surplus. Rents remain in earnings and cash, so no synthetic IndAS lease liability is subtracted; hire-purchase debt is already included once. No value is added for property/equipment already in earnings, no full Vista claim is added in base, no NCI exists, and no dividend is paid while retaining the same cash. Entry EV adds capital creditors still unpaid at entry; terminal EV does not deduct them again after scheduled settlement. The base multiple is an analyst normalization assumption, not a claimed current peer median.

The primary non-rescue base has no reportable conditional IRR because of its reserve breach. Explicit base rescue produces 14.7% conditional annualized return after hypothetical dilution; the ₹1cr-reserve non-rescue alternative gives 14.8%. These do not justify R scoring under the unresolved source gate. Bear rescue gives -6.3%, with materially impaired shareholder wealth. Bull is a high-execution conditional path, not the central valuation.

All cases show 12/15/18% hurdle entry prices only where fully funded. For rescued cases each trial entry price also reprices the placement to 70% of that price, recalculates whole-share dilution and fees, and solves a finite funded bracket with residual checks; these are not fixed-₹80.57-placement counterfactuals; ordinary entry prices remain null. Two-way growth/multiple, working-capital/maintenance, guarantee/reserve and settlement/project-delay grids rerun cash, not just terminal prices. The standard ₹2cr reserve has no valid funded reverse-solver bracket crossing the 15% hurdle, so required growth is not invented. The lower-reserve alternative solves a funded bracket and publishes its residual. This makes the price broadly dependent on fair execution and financing, not an obvious margin of safety.

sections.title: Peer context and SME implementation
sections.text:
The final prospectus reproduces FY26 peer financials: Invicta Diagnostic revenue ₹32.3536cr with 30.17% EBITDA margin, Krsnaa ₹772.7740cr with 27.42%, and Star Imaging ₹88.5269cr with 36.33%. Pramodini's 49.61% is higher, but payer mix, owned equipment versus O&M, staff/lease classification, scale and accounting normalization differ. These figures are issuer-reproduced primary-document comparisons, not independently normalized live peer valuations, and they do not validate an 8× exit multiple or a superior moat.

The official 60-session exchange calendar window contains only 42 issuer observations because listing began on 19 August. Eighteen prelisting absences are not zero-volume sessions. The initial series was ST, changing to SM in September; both issuer observations are retained by ISIN, avoiding the false 32-session history obtained by filtering only current SM. Exact 20-session mean/median traded value is ₹80.94/60.46 lakh; since-listing 42-session mean/median is ₹239.94/77.99 lakh, heavily influenced by listing activity. No complete 60-trading-day issuer history is claimed.

The 19 October lot is 1,200 shares, ₹1,38,120 at the reference close. An illustrative ₹5 lakh position buys three whole lots (₹4,14,360) or requires four lots (₹5,52,480) to reach/exceed it; this is not a suitability recommendation. The 5% participation starting test uses the lower since-listing mean/median, with exact 20-day and 2%/10% checks plus whole-lot capacity. Spreads, one-sided circuits, current surveillance and live depth are unverified. L 7 explicitly discounts the favourable arithmetic for short history and chunky SME lots; G4 remains Conditional. No market maker guarantees an exit.

sections.title: Factor audit, gates and classification
sections.text:
The same 13 canonical factors feed the framework once: governance, moat, revenue growth, runway, capital efficiency, cash conversion, balance sheet, execution, earnings quality, prospective return, downside, price expectations and liquidity. BQS is a business-quality assessment, GQS measures growth quality, and IAS measures a price-dependent investment setup. They are not summed into a super-score. Exact decimal weights, contributions, missing-weight coverage and mathematical bounds are included below; display is half-up to one decimal, while classification retains unrounded values.

G1 is Conditional rather than Fail: related-party allocation and controls need improvement, but no established minority abuse or fraud justifies an avoid-governance conclusion. G2 is Hold for the quantified unresolved guarantee discrepancy and financial verification issues. G3 and G4 are Conditional for funding timing and implementation. G2 excludes numerical quality/growth/investment rankings even though diagnostic BQS/GQS can be computed. R is NS because a source-supported, financeable ordinary base return cannot be established, and IAS remains NS without redistributing its 35% weight.

The earnings/cash positives are not discarded: volume growth is real, normalized operating profit expanded, cumulative cash conversion after supplier-financing correction remains approximately 1.07×, and organic incremental returns are positive. Nor is a small market capitalization automatically disqualifying. The conclusion is Hold — unresolved, not a blanket SME rejection and not an evidence-backed compounder candidate. Factor sensitivity moves the two most judgmental quality factors by ±1; narrow decimal differences should not be over-interpreted.

sections.title: Bear case, falsification and monitoring
sections.text:
The most important thesis variable is cash realization after supplier and related-party claims, not reported procedure growth alone. A credible linked stress is delayed commissioning plus more low-yield procedures, lower staff/equipment utilization, stretched government receivables, mandatory machine replacement and a guarantee call. This can require dilution even while reported operating earnings remain positive. The bear model explicitly funds rescue before cash uses, rather than treating a negative bank balance as a viable investment. Impairment risk is High because the shareholder recovery depends on operating execution and enforceable claims, not merely a temporary quoted drawdown.

The strongest evidence against an overly bearish reading is genuine CT/MRI volume growth, diversified model revenues, original audit no-default statements, approximately 1.07× corrected three-year conversion and meaningful fresh IPO equity. Conversely, the clean main opinion and headline net cash cannot settle the guarantee discrepancy or make earmarked proceeds freely deployable. No speculative 5×/10× target is warranted: five-year 5× and 10× need roughly 38% and 58.5% annualized shareholder growth, above the supported central operating/financing case. The multibagger outcome is speculative/unsupported, not assigned a probability.

Monitor the original FY26 audit annexures; reconciliation of ₹14.15cr versus ₹4.95cr guarantees; Vista loan terms, cash-interest evidence and collections; receivables ageing and PPP receipts; IPO bank-release and utilization statements; vendor settlements/LC conversion; commissioning and unit-level volumes at the four funded centres; normalized margins and recurring maintenance; and lot/circuit/surveillance changes. A quantified resolution and financeable cash bridge could remove Hold, whereas a verified undisclosed guarantee/default, deterioration in aged debt with no recovery, or persistent failure to commission equipment would invalidate the investment thesis. Price volatility alone does not.

sections.title: Evidence, limitations and reproducibility
sections.text:
Primary evidence consists of the final prospectus and examination report, earlier draft restatement, original FY21–FY25 annual financials and audit annexures, issuer annual reports, final allotment announcement, official dated security master and actual exchange ZIP/CSV rows. Every material calculation carries source IDs and page or table locators. Earlier restatement figures are retained as labelled comparisons rather than mixed silently with final figures. Source document hashes preserve exactly which payloads were reviewed. Search snippets and rolling quotes are not substituted for dated filings or tape.

The main remaining information requests are the guarantee reconciliation, original full FY26 audit package, recoverability/terms for related-party claims, actual post-IPO cash and vendor settlement dates, equipment utilization and new-centre cohort economics, and cutoff surveillance/depth. Missing documents are described as not located, not presumed adverse. Financial models are conditional research tools, not audited interim accounts or forecasts endorsed by management. Original statement classifications, analytical reclassifications and forward assumptions remain separate.

The source-safe inputs, complete historical rows, dated funding model, full sensitivity grids and scoring arithmetic are embedded in the canonical record. A compact or full research package can rebuild the calculations after all generated outputs are removed. That reproduces the arithmetic and stated assumptions; it does not independently authenticate source PDFs that are intentionally omitted from distribution. Full PDFs, OCR, shareholder lists and personal identifiers are not part of the research package. This report is analytical research, not personalized financial advice or an instruction to buy or sell.

summary:
Hold — unresolved. Pramodini Medicare Limited, NSE PRAMODINI, ISIN INE2JG601017, CIN U85110AP2000PLC035231, operates diagnostic imaging and laboratories, not inpatient hospitals. It was incorporated in September 2000, changed to public-company status in November 2025 and first appears in the official listed tape on 19 August 2026. The analytical cutoff is 20 October 2026; the authenticated reference quote is the 19 October close of ₹115.10, not a live executable bid. Financials are nominal INR crore unless stated. This report was researched after the cutoff using documents dated on or before it.

A genuine scaling business is visible: revenue expanded from ₹18.56cr in FY21 to ₹62.29cr in FY26, with MRI/CT/private-hospital and PSU activity contributing. However, an unresolved ₹9.20cr difference between the FY25 CARO guarantee total and the latest prospectus disclosures is material relative to equity and available free cash. This is an inconsistency requiring reconciliation, not an allegation of fraud. Vista recoverability, bank-return controls and old equipment payables compound the need for clarification.

BQS and GQS are diagnostic assessments, excluded from quality rankings while G2 is on Hold. R and IAS are NS. Neither an apparently modest earnings multiple nor a conditional spreadsheet outcome cures reliability. The report provides a five-year, cash-linked scenario model but no actionable target price, ordinary expected return or recommendation to transact.
